name: MLP

one.input: 547 features from one current. Each current contributes two 13 × 20 maps, a 13-value frame mask, 13 observation times and one current value.
layers: Dense 547 → 40 (21,920 parameters)

three.input: 1,641 features from three currents, with 547 features per current.
layers: Dense 1,641 → 40 (65,680 parameters)

activation: GELU after each 40-unit hidden layer. Eight output logits pass through sigmoid to yield the four diffusivity and four transference-number Bernstein coefficients.
optimizer: AdamW, initial learning rate 0.001, weight decay 0.01, β₁ = 0.9, β₂ = 0.999, ε = 10⁻⁸. Cosine annealing reaches zero over 2,200 minibatch updates.
training: 100 epochs, batch size 64, shuffled training materials each epoch. Loss is the mean squared error of the eight unit-interval coefficients.
Retain the checkpoint with the lowest coefficient MSE across 156 validation materials. Seed 0 supplies primary results, with repeats at seeds 1 and 2.
notes: The two input maps are concentration deviation (c − 1) and reconstructed velocity. Both use per-current training RMS normalization. The three-current first dense layer adds 43,760 trainable weights. Each domain and current count has separately fitted weights.

name: MLP + test-time training

one.input: 547 features from one current. Each current contributes two 13 × 20 maps, a 13-value frame mask, 13 observation times and one current value.
layers: Dense 547 → 40 (21,920 parameters)

three.input: 1,641 features from three currents, with 547 features per current.
layers: Dense 1,641 → 40 (65,680 parameters)

activation: GELU after each 40-unit hidden layer. Eight output logits pass through sigmoid to yield the four diffusivity and four transference-number Bernstein coefficients.
optimizer: Pretrain for 100 epochs with AdamW at 0.001, batch size 64, and cosine decay to zero. Test-time adaptation uses a fresh AdamW for each material, fixed learning rate 0.00001, weight decay 0.01, β₁ = 0.9, β₂ = 0.999, ε = 10⁻⁸.
training: Start from the matching supervised MLP checkpoint. Run 150 updates on all weights of an independent copy for each test material. The objective is the mean squared concentration-conservation residual over valid time intervals and spatial bins.

Choose the learning rate from 0.00001, 0.0001 and 0.001 on 100 validation materials by median observed-range squared log-diffusivity error. All domain and current-count combinations selected 0.00001 at seed 0. Seeds 1 and 2 reuse that rate.
notes: Parameter counts apply to one independently adapted model. Clean and Gaussian-noisy cases use the same settings. The primary run processed up to 32 independent material fits together on CPU.

name: Fourier neural operator (FNO)

one.input: 6 × 13 × 20 input tensor (channels × frames × spatial bins). Five channels for the current plus one shared spatial coordinate.
layers: 1 × 1 convolution lifts 6 → 11 channels (77 parameters). Pad the grid to 16 × 24.
Four Fourier blocks, each 11 → 11 channels (14,652 real parameters per block). Each sums a spectral convolution and a parallel 1 × 1 convolution.
Crop to 13 × 20. A 1 × 1 convolution projects 11 → 22 channels (264).
Masked mean and max pooling concatenate 22 + 22 = 44 features. Dense head 44 → 128 (5,760) → 8 (1,032).

three.input: 16 × 13 × 20 input tensor. Five channels for each of three currents plus one shared spatial coordinate.
layers: 1 × 1 convolution lifts 16 → 11 channels (187 parameters). Pad to 16 × 24.
Four Fourier blocks, each 11 → 11 channels (14,652 real parameters per block).
Crop to 13 × 20. A 1 × 1 convolution projects 11 → 22 channels (264).
Masked mean and max pooling produce 44 features. Dense head 44 → 128 (5,760) → 8 (1,032).

activation: GELU follows Fourier blocks 1–3, the 11 → 22 projection and the 128-unit dense layer. Block 4 feeds the projection directly. Sigmoid maps the eight output logits to coefficients.
optimizer: AdamW, initial learning rate 0.001, weight decay 0.01, β₁ = 0.9, β₂ = 0.999, ε = 10⁻⁸. Cosine annealing reaches zero over 2,200 minibatch updates.
training: 100 epochs, batch size 64, shuffled training materials each epoch. Loss is the mean squared error of the eight unit-interval coefficients.
Retain the checkpoint with the lowest coefficient MSE across 156 validation materials. Seed 0 supplies primary results, with repeats at seeds 1 and 2.
notes: Each current contributes c − 1, reconstructed velocity, a validity mask, observation time and current magnitude. Each Fourier block learns two complex 11 × 11 × 5 × 6 weight banks for opposite temporal frequency bands. Each complex entry counts as two real trainable scalars. The ten extra lift channels add 110 weights for three currents. Clean and Gaussian-noisy runs use the same layer shapes for a given count.
